meta.title: How to get a Lumen Bay library card (sample)
meta.subtitle: A made-up guide to a made-up library, to show how this explainer template works.
meta.description: SAMPLE CONTENT – NOT REAL. A fictional explainer about getting a library card in the imaginary town of Lumen Bay.

intro.heading: Can you get a library card, and what do you need?
body: **This is sample content. Lumen Bay, its library, its rules and its "Bay Tokens" are all made up.** Nothing here is real advice about anything.
Answer a few quick questions to get a personalized result, a checklist of what to bring, the important dates, and answers to common questions.

questions.help: Lumen Bay is an imaginary seaside town.

options.label: Outside Lumen Bay, but I work or study there

questions.text: Do you have a document with your name and Lumen Bay address?
questions.help: For example, a (fictional) Lighthouse Water bill or a rental agreement.

options.label: No, or not in my name

questions.text: Have you had a Lumen Bay library card before?

options.label: No, this is my first one

questions.text: What would you like to borrow?
questions.help: Pick as many as you like.

options.label: Seeds from the Seed Library
options.help: Plant them, then return a few seeds next season.

options.label: The Star Kit
options.help: A small telescope with a sky map.

resultBlocks.title: You qualify for a free Full Card
resultBlocks.body: As a Lumen Bay resident, your Full Card is free. It lets you borrow up to 12 items at a time.

resultBlocks.title: No address document? Use a Kindly Neighbor Letter
resultBlocks.body: Ask anyone with a Lumen Bay Full Card to fill in a Kindly Neighbor Letter saying you live in town. The library has blank letters at the front desk.

resultBlocks.title: You can get a Neighbor Card
resultBlocks.body: Because you work or study in Lumen Bay, you can get a Neighbor Card. It costs **10 Bay Tokens a year** and lets you borrow up to 6 items at a time.

resultBlocks.title: You can get a Visitor Pass (reading room only)
resultBlocks.body: Visitors can't take items home, but a free Visitor Pass lets you read anything inside the library and use the computers for 1 hour a day. Bring a photo ID.

resultBlocks.title: A grown-up needs to co-sign
resultBlocks.body: If you're under 18, a parent or guardian must come with you and sign the card form. Under-12s get a Junior Card with a sticker map of the library.

resultBlocks.title: Renewing is quick
resultBlocks.body: You don't need a new card. Bring your old card to any desk and it's renewed on the spot. Expired cards keep your borrowing history.

resultBlocks.title: Replacing a lost card costs 2 Bay Tokens
resultBlocks.body: Report the lost card first so nobody else can use it. A replacement costs 2 Bay Tokens, even for free cards, and keeps your card number.

resultBlocks.title: The Star Kit needs an adult card
resultBlocks.body: Only Full or Neighbor Card holders aged 18+ can borrow the Star Kit. A grown-up can borrow it for the family on their own card.

resultBlocks.title: Here's the general guide
resultBlocks.body: Your situation is a bit unusual. Read the checklist and FAQ below, or ask at the (fictional) front desk.

resultBlocks.title: Everything at a glance
resultBlocks.body: Residents get a free Full Card, people who work or study in town can get a Neighbor Card, and visitors get a Visitor Pass. Under-18s need a grown-up to co-sign.

rules.note: Visitors: show only the visitor pass and stop.

checklist.heading: What to bring
checklist.intro: Tick things off as you go. Your ticks aren't saved anywhere — print the list if you want to keep it.

items.text: Document with your Lumen Bay address
items.detail: A Lighthouse Water bill or rental agreement, dated within the last 3 months.
Signed by someone who already has a Full Card.

items.text: Proof you work or study in Lumen Bay
items.detail: A company ID or school enrollment slip.

items.text: 10 Bay Tokens for the yearly fee
2 Bay Tokens for the replacement card
A parent or guardian, plus their ID
A small envelope for your seeds
items.detail: The Seed Library runs out of envelopes on weekends.

items.text: A reusable bag for your books

items.title: Story Fair sign-ups
items.description: Sign-ups for this year's fair have closed. It's here to show how a past date looks.

items.title: Free Card Week ends
items.description: During Free Card Week, the Neighbor Card fee is waived.

items.title: Seed Library returns are due
items.description: Bring back a few seeds from what you grew, so others can borrow them next season.

items.title: Summer Reading Quest starts
items.description: Read 5 books, get a (fictional) lighthouse pin.

items.question: Is any of this real?
items.answer: No. Lumen Bay, its library, the Bay Tokens and every rule on this page are invented to demonstrate the explainer template.

items.question: How long does it take to get the card?
items.answer: About 10 minutes at the front desk, if you bring everything on the checklist.

items.question: Can I borrow e-books?
items.answer: Yes. Full and Neighbor Card holders can borrow up to 3 e-books at a time from the (fictional) Lumen Cloud shelf.

items.question: What if I return the Star Kit late?
answer: There's no fine, but you can't borrow the Star Kit again for one month.
_Stars will still be there next month._

items.question: Are my answers saved?
items.answer: No. Your answers stay in this browser tab and disappear when you close it. They are never sent to anyone.
